subject: Acme: Redwood POC kickoff - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-04T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme discovery recap + proposed POC kickoff (Mar 11)

Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps for the POC kickoff: 

Pain points you confirmed:
- Inconsistent retrieval latency on your search index when serving LLM-powered answers (spikes during business hours).
- High per-token cost for long-context QA currently driving down throughput.
- Need reproducible evaluation to measure answer accuracy vs. current rules-based system.

Goals for the 4-week POC:
1) Reduce median response latency for 512-token windows from ~850ms to <450ms under typical load.
2) Demonstrate 30% reduction in per-token cost via batching + KV caching without dropping accuracy (accept <=5% accuracy delta on our eval set).
3) Build an evaluation set and baseline prompts so we can measure regressions.

Scope / owners:
- Redwood will deliver a hosted POC environment (Dedicated trial) and run model variants we discussed.
  - Owner: Marissa Cole (redwood) — project lead / weekly syncs
- Infra & access (data pipeline + VPC peering if needed): Aditya Rao (redwood) — will provision access and coordinate auth
- Success metrics & quality evals: Rishi Malhotra (redwood) — will own prompt set and evaluation harness
- Acme will provide: sample dataset (500-2k anonymized queries + expected answers), API endpoint for live traffic replay, and security questionnaire answers

Metrics & evals:
- Latency: p50/p95 for 128/512 token spans under defined QPS (we'll include synthetic load).
- Cost: tokens/second and cost per 1k tokens measured across runs and model variants.
- Quality: prompt/eval set (we'll run Rouge/BLEU + custom semantic matches you outlined).

Proposed timeline:
- Mar 6: Acme shares sample data + security questionnaire answers
- Mar 9: Redwood completes initial infra setup and shares access details
- Mar 11: POC kickoff call + align on final prompt set and acceptance criteria
- Mar 11–Apr 8: 4-week run + weekly syncs (Wednesdays)

Access/setup steps (high level):
- Provide service account for S3 access (or share CSV) + API keys for traffic replay
- Complete basic security questionnaire so we can enable Dedicated trial account
- We'll provide a short onboarding doc and a small helper script to push sample data

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (POC plan, owners, timeline) and data_schema.csv (expected sample format).

Please confirm the proposed kickoff date (Mar 11) and whether the sample dataset will be ready by Mar 6. Happy to adjust dates if needed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (12 KB)]
[Attachment: data_schema.csv (3 KB)]

Subject: Re: Acme discovery recap + proposed POC kickoff (Mar 11)

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap, that matches our notes. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Metrics: The most important KPI for us is p95 under 100 QPS during business hours. If you can include both p50/p95 that works.
2) Eval set: we'll provide ~1,000 anonymized queries from production logs (filters applied). Expect to have that ready by Mar 6 — I'll confirm by EOD tomorrow.
3) Security: Our security team will want to run through your SOC2 evidence — should we send them to security@acme.com or have them use your security portal?

Mar 11 kickoff looks good from our side. Nina will coordinate internal attendees.

One more ask: can you include a short section in the POC plan on rollback/fallback behavior if latency degrades in prod? That will help our platform team.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Search & Knowledge 
Acme Corp

Tom — great, thanks for the confirmations. Quick updates based on your notes and Nina's expected attendees: 

- We'll add p95 @ 100 QPS to the primary acceptance criteria and include both p50/p95 in the dashboard.
- Security: please point your security team to our portal (https://security.redwood.com/clients/acme) — I'll also attach a SOC2 evidence bundle and a short FAQ about our Dedicated trial security controls. If they prefer email, send to security@redwood.com and we'll route internally.
- Rollback/fallback section: added. Brief summary: canary traffic split, automatic fallback to a cheaper compatible model variant, and circuit-breaker for high tail latency. Full details in the attached POC kickoff recap doc.

POC kickoff recap (high level):
- Kickoff call: Mar 11, 10:00 AM PT — invite to follow once Tom confirms attendees
- Immediate asks from Acme before kickoff:
  1) Share anonymized sample dataset (S3 link or CSV) by Mar 6
  2) Add redwood-poc@acme.com (service account) to any internal Slack channel for quick coordination (optional)
  3) Complete short security intake (link above)

Prompt set / evals:
- We'll prepare an initial prompt set of 300 queries (subset of your 1k) for baseline runs and 700 for full evaluation. Rishi will share the evaluation harness and acceptance script early next week.

Owners & contact points:
- Marissa Cole (redwood) — POC lead, syncs, and success criteria
- Aditya Rao (redwood) — infra, access, peering, keys
- Rishi Malhotra (redwood) — evaluation harness, prompt set, quality monitoring
- Tom Reynolds / Nina Patel (acme) — product + platform owners

Attachments: poc-kickoff-recap.docx (detailed plan) and eval_prompt_set.csv (initial prompt seed).

I'll send calendar invites once I get confirmation on attendees. Looking forward to kicking off.

Best,
